content:
Apple has shared more details about the AI labelling requirements it announced for Apple Music back in March. Here's what to know.

AI-generated content will be clearly labelled on Apple Music

Apple announced earlier this year that Apple Music would require AI transparency disclosures for new cover art, songs, compositions, and music videos uploaded to the platform.

Apple has now shared further details on how this mechanism will actually work in practice.

In an email to creators sent today, Apple said: "Later this year, we'll also start surfacing these tags to Apple Music listeners as 'Made With AI' labels."

Apple also clarified when these disclosures apply. The email reads:

Apple Music added that the goal of the move is "maximum transparency for listeners as much as possible," and pointed creators to its music style guide for more information.

Apple Music's approach is just the latest example of streaming platforms grappling with the surge of AI-generated music, as more and more artists begin incorporating generative AI into their production processes.

Spotify previously said it would not include AI-actor music in its editorial or algorithmic recommendations by default; Deezer also announced last year that fully AI-generated songs would be excluded from its recommendations and editorial playlists. Last month, Deezer also reported that fully AI-generated music surpassed 50% of daily new uploads for the first time.

On the Apple Music side, platform head Oliver Schusser recently appeared on Billboard's "On the Record" podcast, where he noted that while more than a third of all music uploaded to Apple Music each month is fully AI-generated, it accounts for less than 0.5% of overall streams on the platform.
